title: References
text:
Students are expected to be comfortable with college-level mathematics and science and are strongly encouraged to consult reliable reference texts. For example, foundational and practical texts in mathematics, applied thermodynamics and computational tools, including Bird (2021), Hannah & Hillier (1995), Russell et al. (2021), Bolton (2021), Shaw (2017), Sweigart (2021), and Sweigart (2020).




References

Bird, J. O. (2021). Bird’s engineering mathematics (9th ed.). Routledge.

Sweigart, A. (2021). Beyond the basic stuff with python. No Starch Press.

title: Syllabus
text:
2 Learning Objectives
Students will be able to: 1. Simulate steady-state and transient operation of thermal power plants. 2. Analyze the performance of boilers, turbines, condensers, and feedwater systems. 3. Optimize plant efficiency and evaluate environmental performance. 4. Diagnose and troubleshoot common operational issues.

title: Thermal Power Plant Simulator
text:
This course provides hands-on training in the simulation, operation, and optimization of thermal power plants using industry-standard simulation software.
Instructor: Serhat Beyenir
Schedule: 4 periods per week (September – December 2026)
Format: Lectures + Simulations



Dynamic simulation of Rankine and combined cycles
Plant performance analysis and optimization
Fault detection and troubleshooting scenarios
Efficiency and environmental impact assessment
